title: McDonalds Has Secretly Deployed AI Models to Determine Exactly What to Charge You for Its Mid Fast Food Burgers
key_facts: Reuters investigation: McDonald's uses AI models to set menu prices across the US.
The system estimates what each store's customers will pay, from millions of daily transactions, for nearly 14,000 restaurants.
Three franchisees told Reuters the system widened price gaps between nearby restaurants.
Reuters found Big Macs at $5.69 in one Fresno store and $6.89 at another two miles away (21%).
McDonald's called the portal a 'tool, not a mandate'; several franchisees said they felt pressured.
McDonald's takes a cut of revenue, not profit; AI has recently recommended some price cuts, causing friction.
Corporate tracks 'pricing non-compliance'; AI firm Tiger Analytics works with it.
quote_evidence: McDonald's insisted that the AI pricing portal is a "tool, not a mandate."
CEO Chris Kempczinski reportedly told investors that "pricing non-compliance" is now a consideration in how it reviews franchisees.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-set prices vary store to store and franchisees feel pressure to follow them.
event_date: Reuters report, date not stated; Futurism 4 Oct 2026
notes: Original Reuters article not opened; facts via Futurism, which writes in a sarcastic tone (ignored).
